audit_name: Cover-Hart Asymptotic Relationship & Bayes Error Ceiling Forensic Audit

investigated_claim.claim_text: The Bayes error rate of the 3-class problem on this dataset is bounded below by R* >= 28.0%, making 80%+ accuracy mathematically impossible.

forensic_audit_findings.finding_1_parameter_provenance: The 0.44 parameter was NOT the error rate of an asymptotic 1-Nearest Neighbor classifier. It was an approximation of the finite-sample empirical accuracy (44.60%) or error (1 - 0.56) of a parametric logistic regression model fitted on contrastive embeddings on N=296 pairs.

finding_2_cover_hart_assumptions_violate.asymptotic_infinite_sample_assumption: VIOLATED. Cover-Hart (1967) theorem applies strictly in the large-sample limit (N -> infinity). N=296 is a small, finite, clustered sample.
finding_2_cover_hart_assumptions_violate.classifier_identity_assumption: VIOLATED. The theorem establishes a relationship between the 1-NN risk R_NN and the Bayes risk R*. Substituting the risk of a linear logistic classifier into the 1-NN bound is a severe mathematical category error.
finding_2_cover_hart_assumptions_violate.metric_space_density_assumption: VIOLATED. Textual pairs embedded via neural networks on discrete vocabulary do not satisfy the required continuous distribution assumptions.

forensic_audit_findings.finding_3_category_error: An empirical error of a specific candidate classifier cannot be used to bound the Bayes error of the underlying data-generating distribution. An unoptimized or noisy model achieving 56% error implies nothing about the theoretical ceiling of an optimal classifier.

certified_scientific_corrections.retraction_statement: The mathematical claim that the Bayes error rate is at least 28.0% and that 80%+ accuracy is mathematically impossible is officially retracted as scientifically unfounded.
certified_scientific_corrections.scientifically_defensible_limitations_st: Empirical results to date peak at 50.26% on the official held-out test and 47.64% on dual-unseen validation. Reaching 80%+ accuracy remains unachieved due to documented empirical factors: (1) high label noise and conflicting annotations in the original Kaggle dataset, (2) severe class boundary ambiguity surrounding Potential Fit, and (3) omission of critical non-resume hiring signals (e.g. interview evaluations, salary alignment, visa eligibility). However, 80%+ accuracy is not proven to be mathematically impossible, and remains an objective for future research with cleaner, multi-modal hiring data.
